summary: Fujio Taniguchi worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earning a PhD from Nagoya University in 1991 under Musashi Tachikawa and other scholars. A former professor at Nagoya Women's University, he is attested at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute in 2026.

Fulgence Fresnel worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the Maronite College (Pontifical Maronite College) in 1826 and was a pupil of Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy around 1823–1838.

Fumi Yao specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Tokyo by 2011. She served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo in 2023 and is attested at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute in 2026.

Fumihiko Sueki works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his BA and doctorates at the University of Tokyo under Yoshiro Tamura, Kyosho Hayashima, and Hajime Nakamura, later serving as Tokyo professor (1995–2009) and Nichibunken professor (~2009–2015).

Fumihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 2015) and held an appointment as a specially appointed associate professor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Fumimaro Watanabe studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto, where he earned his PhD in 1976 under Anthony Kennedy Warder. He later served as professor at Kindai University (1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (1987).
Fumio Enomoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1980–1984) and as a professor at Osaka University (~1999–2017).

Fumio Masutani worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies, receiving a doctorate from the University of Tokyo in 1961. He was a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1949–1965) and Taisho University (~1968–1973), and president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).

Fumio Matsuda works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Komazawa University and served as an executive committee chair for the Association for the Study of Indian Religions in 1997.

Fumio Ouchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He obtained his doctorate from Otani University, where he served as associate professor (~1993–2000) and professor (~2000–2013).
Fumio Shoji specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University, where he later served as an assistant professor (~2014–2018) and associate professor from around 2018.
Fumio Tamamuro is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Meiji University from around 1954 to 1958 and later held a post there from around 1975 to 2006.

Futoshi Omae specializes in Indology and philosophy. He held posts as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1990–1991), and at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing (attested 1997) and Shimane International Junior College (attested 1998).

Futoshi Takehashi specializes in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Otani University (attested 1992) and served as an assistant at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute from 1995 to 1997.
Fuyuan Luo works in Tibetology and religious studies. Attested as a PhD student under doctoral supervisor Adam Yuet Chau at the University of Cambridge in 2026, he also held a post there.

Fyodor Buslaev worked in linguistics and history. He studied at Moscow State University under Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov (~1834–1838), graduating in 1843, and held positions there from 1846, becoming an adjunkt in 1850.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Georg Bühler and Hermann Jacobi, later serving as docent and full professor at Saint Petersburg State University from 1901 to 1930.

Félicien de Saulcy worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the École polytechnique (1826–1828), the artillery and engineering school in Metz (1828–1830), and was a student of Eugène Burnouf.

Félix Lacôte was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD from the University of Paris in 1908, studying under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet, and became a professor at the University of Lyon in 1911.

Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist who studied at KU Leuven, University of Bonn, University of Munich, and University of Paris under Eugène Burnouf and Christian Lassen. He spent his career at KU Leuven as professor from 1841 to 1877.
